source_result: GMI-DA3 of GMI_DOMAIN_ALGEBRA_EXECUTED_V1 section 4 (gap DG-3, and gap G8's demand for lower bounds rather than occupancy alone): the crossover of the lazy/eager duality GMI-DA2 is H*(d) = [(R^d*F - (R+F))*bits + R^d*F*D*d]/(d*D) ~ R^d/d, unbounded in structure depth, so the bounded reduction that reduced DC1 (RV-377-044) exists at every FIXED depth and no single reuse horizon amortizes it over a family of unbounded depth. That has stood as a remark; this record turns it into an executed kingdom decision, and it is the first time the depth family is run against a PARENT-MAXIMAL opponent as protocol rule 19 (gap DG-5) requires
original_hypothesis: The depth escape of GMI-DA3 is NOT a property of the binding carrier: it is a property of the binding OPERATOR, and GMI-DA3's formula silently assumes that the opponent must materialize R^d * F distinct bound vectors. Whether it must is measurable. The XOR bind that RV-377-044 actually executed is commutative and involutive, so a role path composes to the PARITY of its role multiset and the number of distinct path vectors is at most 2^R, saturating with depth; an opponent that materializes one bundle per DISTINCT path vector therefore has a description bounded UNIFORMLY in depth, which closes the escape for that operator. Adding the PERMUTE primitive that DC1's declared native basis already contains (role at path position i protected by the cyclic shift rho^i) makes the path code injective and restores an R^d binding set, and there the escape survives even against the strongest opponent we can build. In neither case does the carrier occupy a frontier cell that the parent-maximal opponent cannot occupy, so neither yields a kingdom at scope
minimal_proposed_change: gmi_microscope/dk_depth.py: an exact charged microscope over E_rolefill(R = 4 roles, F = 8 fillers, k = 3 bound items per record, 8 development and 8 evaluation records on unseen structures) at structure depths d = 1..6, two hypervector widths D = 64 and D = 128, three record seeds (7, 13, 23) at D = 64 and one (7) at D = 128, under two declared binding laws XOR and PERM: 48 cells, six rows each. Same universe as every DC receipt: TOTAL_BITS 8, FRAC_BITS 4, basis B0, theta = 0.85, C = desc + H*exec_q + r*(upd_e + ver_e) + (r/4)*rev_e with r = 0. new_prediction_before_outcome: FRONTIER RULE for every clause that mentions a frontier, occupancy or a crossover (protocol rule 17): a row OCCUPIES reuse horizon H of a cell iff (a) it is ADMISSIBLE there, i.e. its exact rational correct/total >= theta = 85/100, and (b) its exact rational lifecycle C(H) = desc + compile + H * exec_q equals the minimum C(H) over the admissible rows of that cell; ties occupy jointly. This is the best-admissible-cost rule at a fixed obligation, not a largest-ladder-size rule: every row answers the same query set. A CELL is one (law, depth, width, record seed) configuration; a row OCCUPIES A CELL when it occupies at least one reuse horizon of that cell's extended grid. In all 48 cells the four rows VSA, STORE_MAT, STORE_PATH and STORE_DEDUP have EQUAL answer signatures, and VSA_NOBIND's differs from VSA's in all 48. new_falsifier: Any single cell, under either declared price vector, in which the binding carrier occupies at least one reuse horizon of the extended grid and NO parent row occupies ANY reuse horizon of that same extended grid, falsifies clause 9 and establishes a depth-gated kingdom at that depth (d_star), at which point criteria 5 and 6 - neutral biosphere recovery and recurrence under remint and independent search encodings - become due. Separately: any PERM cell whose parent-maximal crossover differs from the exact rational listed in clause 6 falsifies the cost algebra; any XOR cell of depth >= 3 whose parent-maximal store exceeds 4618 bits (D = 64) falsifies clause 3 and with it the claim that the XOR family admits a single depth-uniform bounded reduction; and any cell whose reuse grid fails to reach twice its largest crossover falsifies clause 5 and re-opens gap DG-2.

failure_class: Clause 7's two wrong ratios are an ARITHMETIC ERROR IN THE FROZEN RECORD, caught by the executed run; the executed crossovers themselves matched the closed forms exactly. Clauses 6b, 8 and 12's third conjunct are OVER-CONFIDENT PREDICTIONS about admissibility and about which cells would be measurable: each assumed a cell would be admissible where the ecology's own draw made it not. Clause 9's failing conjunct is a SPECIFICATION ERROR in the clause, not a surprise in the world: 'a parent occupies every cell' is false wherever NOTHING occupies the cell, and the clause should have been stated over the decisions with a non-empty admissible set, where it holds 62 of 62.
strongest_mundane_explanation: The lazy/eager trade is a memoization trade and nothing more: a carrier that composes on demand is smaller and slower than one that stores the composites, and which wins is a reuse-horizon question. The only thing depth changes is HOW MANY composites there are, and that is a property of the binding operator's algebra, not of the idea of binding
strongest_parent_explanation: The caching/compilation literature: time-memory trade-offs are indexed by the size of the memoized domain, and an operator with a small image (XOR binding: the image is the group generated by the role vectors, of size 2^R) has a bounded memo table however deep the expressions are. The VSA literature's own use of PERMUTE for position protection is the acknowledgement that XOR binding alone does not encode order or depth
measurement_validity_status: Valid at the declared scope: exact charged replay, exact rational admissibility and exact rational frontier comparisons, deterministic receipt (byte reproducible from the committed file). Three limits are stated rather than hidden. (i) The theta = 0.85 gate silences 34 of the 96 decisions, all of them XOR cells whose path code collapses; the kingdom verdict therefore rests on the 62 decisions with a non-empty frontier. (ii) The native price vector leaves the opponent's materialization unpriced, which is the reading most favourable to the opponent and is used deliberately so the negative verdict is conservative. (iii) One declared codebook, one k, one obligation family; the replication axis executed here is three record seeds at D = 64 and a second width, not a second codebook.
mechanism_attribution: The depth escape of GMI-DA3 is an algebraic property of the binding operator's IMAGE, not of the binding carrier. XOR binding is commutative and involutive, so the composition of a role path lies in the GF(2) span of the R role vectors: at most 2^R = 16 values, and at most 2^(R-1) = 8 for a fixed depth parity. An opponent that materializes one bundle per DISTINCT composition therefore has a store bounded by 2^R * F vectors HOWEVER DEEP the family goes, which is why its description saturates at 4618 bits at D = 64 while GMI-DA3's formula asks for R^d * F. Protecting the role at path position i with the cyclic shift rho^i - the PERMUTE primitive DC1's declared native basis already contains - makes the path code injective, restores an R^d image, and with it restores an unbounded H*(d) ~ R^d / (d - 1) even against the strongest opponent we could build. In both codes the carrier and the opponent answer identically, so the depth axis moves the PRICE of the reduction and never its existence.
new_invariant_learned: For a superposition carrier over R roles and F fillers at structure depth d, the parent-maximal exemplar store holds |image of the path code| * F vectors, not R^d * F. Executed values: the XOR code's image is min(R^d, 2^(R-1) or 2^R by depth parity) - measured 4, 7, 8, 8, 8, 8 - and the permutation-protected code's image is exactly R^d - measured 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096. The parent-maximal reuse crossover follows: bounded by its depth-1 value under XOR (<= 54.5 at D = 64) and growing as H*(d) ~ R^d/(d-1) under PERM, with executed consecutive ratios 3.5549, 3.7496, 3.8498, 3.9029 rising towards R = 4 and never reaching it. A second invariant, from clause 10: at depth 1 the path-materializing opponent IS the carrier - same description, same serve cost, same answers - so a depth-1 experiment cannot distinguish a binding carrier from an exemplar store at all.
new_theory_constraint: GMI-DA3 must be restated. Its H*(d) = [(R^d*F - (R+F))*bits + R^d*F*D*d]/(d*D) is the crossover against an opponent that materializes R^d * F bindings, and that opponent is parent-maximal only when the binding operator's path code is INJECTIVE. For the XOR operator the formula overstates the parent-maximal store by R^d / |image| = 1, 16/7, 8, 32, 128, 512 at depths 1..6 and the parent-maximal crossover by 6.5957 at the one depth-2 cell where the comparison is measurable; RV-377-044's published depth-2 description ratio of 10.667 becomes 4.6667. Consequently GMI_STRUCTURAL_DOMAINS_KINGDOMS_V1 section 14 criterion 3 (gap DG-3) must name THREE quantities and not one: the family's structure-depth bound, the binding operator whose path code fixes how the opponent's store grows with that depth, and the reuse-horizon bound over which the frontier is read. Under all three named, the criterion is decidable, and here it is decided against the candidate at every executed depth.
